text:
mike-cust: Hey team — we're seeing a spike in generation latency for our Dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-22). p95 from 120ms -> ~2.1s, p99 ~4.7s starting ~08:10 UTC. No change on our end. Any insight?

sara-support: Thanks Mike — sorry about that. Can you confirm this is the dedicated pool we provisioned (ded-22) and whether this is consistent across models?

mike-cust: Yes, ded-22. Happens across rredwood-3b and rredwood-7b. Throughput is normal but single-request latency jumps. We saw a few 429s around the same time.

sara-support: Noted. Adding eng/runtime and oncall. @ben-runtime @luis-oncall tagging.

ben-runtime: I'm on it. First guess is noisy neighbor GPU contention in the dedicated pool. Any chance other tenants on same nodes are running large-batch reranking or long-context jobs?

mike-cust: We only use the pool for steady traffic, batch_size=1 normally. We do have some bursts but nothing sustained. We got some CUDA OOM logs yesterday but ops said they weren't from our jobs.

infra-bot: [automated] ded-22 node group status: 3 nodes (h100-2x) active, MIG config: mixed 1g.5gb + 2g.10gb. Average GPU util 42%, p95 latency alert fired.

luis-oncall: Can you paste a short repro that hits the pool? We want to run a controlled test.

mike-cust: Sure — curl example:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" 
  -H "X-Redwood-Pool: ded-22" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rredwood-7b","input":"Summarize this...","max_tokens":512,"batch_size":1}'

ben-runtime: Running a synthetic run now against ded-22. I'll run `nvidia-smi dmon` and NVML counters to correlate GPU mem/bandwidth.

ben-runtime: Observed on node h100-node-02: sudden PCIe bandwidth saturation and NVLink traffic spikes coinciding with high p99. GPU memory usage looked fine per-process but SM utilization jumped to 96% for a different tenant (tenant-id t-990). That tenant is running large-batch 64 inference jobs.

sara-support: So co-located tenant is causing contention for SM and PCIe, not memory. That matches p99 latency & 429s (queue backs up).

amy-platform: Quick note: autoscaler for dedicated pools uses a 2m moving average of queue length and scales nodes at threshold Q>200. Short bursts of noise won't trigger scale, so interference persists until bursts subside.

luis-oncall: We're seeing MIG placement mixing smaller MIG slices (1g.5gb) and larger 2g.10gb on the same node. Noisy tenant has pinned to larger MIG profiles which still share the same physical SMs and some NVLink resources on H100.

ben-runtime: Repro steps I used locally: 1) Start a helper client that sends continuous batch=64 requests to pool ded-22; 2) Meanwhile run single user requests (batch=1) — observe multi-second p99s. I can attach logs.

ben-runtime: Snippet I used (python):

```
import requests
for i in range(5000):
  requests.post(url, headers=headers, json={"model":"rredwood-7b","input":"x","max_tokens":128,"batch_size":64})
```

ben-runtime: When noisy client is running, p95 for batch=1 jumps from 140ms -> 1.8s; p99 ~4.5s. GPU util for noisy tenant ~98% and co-tenant spikes in stalled cycles.

sara-support: Ok. Short-term mitigation options?

amy-platform: We can: 1) Temporarily evict noisy tenant workloads from ded-22 (requires infra action + ownership confirmation). 2) Change placement policy for tier to one-tenant-per-node for high-isolation pools (will reduce density). 3) Reconfigure MIG flavors to avoid mixed MIGs on same physical GPU (harder but doable). 4) Lower per-tenant concurrency/batch caps at API layer.

luis-oncall: For immediate relief I recommend throttling tenant t-990 (cap their concurrency) and moving it off ded-22. Also bump autoscaler sensitivity to detect short spikes (change to 30s EWMA or add instantaneous max trigger).

ben-runtime: I already opened a node-eviction ticket and started throttling their ingress at the router (rate-limit rule id rl-559). Confirmed reduced batch 64 ingress to 1 req/sec.

mike-cust: Thanks — after you applied the throttle p95 dropped back to ~150ms within 45s. Appreciate the quick response.

sara-support: Great. Action items: 
- ben-runtime: complete eviction + relocation for t-990 (owner)
- amy-platform: schedule MIG reconfiguration proposal for ded pools (owner)
- luis-oncall: adjust autoscaler MR to add short-burst detection (owner)
- support: notify affected customers and deadlines (sara-support)

ben-runtime: I'll follow up in infra ticket #INF-7124 with exact nodes moved and time window. Tentative plan: avoid colocating >1 large-batch tenant per physical GPU, add soft anti-affinity rule.

amy-platform: For medium term, propose a new isolation SKU "dedicated-highiso" which enforces one-tenant-per-node + strict MIG tiling. Will draft RFC by EOW.

luis-oncall: MR for autoscaler prepared, will run canary on staging today. If green we'll roll to prod next week.

sara-support: I'll send a customer note to Mike and any other affected teams summarizing root cause (noisy neighbor SM/NVLink contention on mixed MIG nodes) and the timeline for the platform fixes.

mike-cust: Thanks all. Please cc me on the customer note.

ben-runtime: Final note: short-term remediation (throttle + evict) resolved perf within 1min. Medium-term (MIG tiling + autoscaler changes + isolation SKU) planned. Will update INF-7124 and platform RFC. :white_check_mark:

sara-support: Closing this thread for now — reopening if we see recurrence. Thanks team :thumbsup:
